question: Should `decision: null` on `plugin.approval.resolved` be the permanent public cancellation signal for plugin approval cleanup?
rationale: The PR widens a plugin SDK/gateway event contract, and repository policy treats plugin API changes as compatibility-sensitive without maintainer-confirmed direction.

options.title: Adopt nullable resolved cancellation
options.body: Treat `decision: null` as the supported terminal cancellation event, but require sibling waiter coverage, SDK/docs or contract tests, and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Use a narrower cleanup contract
options.body: Keep resolved decisions non-null and redesign cancellation around a separate internal cleanup/removal event or method contract.

options.title: Land only the before_tool_call path
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept the partial fix, but the linked stale-approval issue should remain open for other approval requesters.

recommendation.title: Adopt nullable resolved cancellation
recommendation.body: Treat `decision: null` as the supported terminal cancellation event, but require sibling waiter coverage, SDK/docs or contract tests, and real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the original plugin approval gateway/API feature and are the strongest history signal for the contract decision.
